text:
Ops Lead: seeing 5xx spike from apac clients starting ~2003456600, lots of retries in the app logs.
SRE Oncall: confirmed, per-metric: GPU pool apac-ml-1 dropped healthy nodes before traffic shift. 500s correlate with failed backend healthchecks.
NetEng: traceroutes look fine but DNS lookups are resolving to old egress IPs for some resolvers. suspect propagation lag after yesterday's failover.
Maya: running `dig +short @8.8.8.8 inference.redwood.example.com` returns the secondary region IP, but our edge range still has some resolvers returning the primary (draining) IP.
Jun: exact cmd and snippet:
```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 inference.redwood.example.com
203.0.113.45
```
SRE Oncall: TTL was lowered to 60s in the playbook earlier this morning but some ISPs ignore low TTLs or have resolver caches with minimum TTL clamps. that explains the mixed results.
Ops Lead: what's our safe mitigation path? we need to reduce errors quickly without making DNS churn worse.
NetEng: propose immediate traffic shift at the LB level to prefer healthy pool (apac-secondary) and leave DNS alone for now. set LB weight 90 -> secondary.
Alice: +1 on LB weight shift. I can apply a gradual weight change. doing 60/40 now to avoid capacity shock.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaled apac-secondary-gpu from 3 -> 7 nodes (requested by Alice) :rocket:
Ben: remind: shifting LB weights is fast, DNS changes are slow. only change DNS if LB shift insufficient and we accept a round of resolver churn.
Maya: if we do alter DNS, we should update both public and split-horizon internal zones. internal resolvers are still returning the old IP because of long-lived records.
NetEng: steps if we must touch DNS:
1) open a transaction
2) change A record to secondary pool IPs
3) commit and watch resolver mix
Example (gcloud):
```
$ gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=redwood-main
$ gcloud dns record-sets transaction remove --name=inference.redwood.example.com. --ttl=300 --type=A 198.51.100.23 --zone=redwood-main
$ gcloud dns record-sets transaction add --name=inference.redwood.example.com. --ttl=60 --type=A 203.0.113.45 --zone=redwood-main
$ gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=redwood-main
```
SRE Oncall: caution: many resolvers ignore TTL drops below 300s, so changing TTLs won't immediate flush caches. also watch negative caching (`SOA`'s `MINIMUM`) if a record gets removed briefly.
Jun: alternative quick trick: pre-warm and prime edges by making healthcheck and probe traffic from known resolvers. do `dig` from multiple public resolvers and our own forwarders to measure propagation.
Alice: I started LB shift to 60/40 at 2003456702. monitoring errors.
SRE Oncall: error rate halved within 40s, latency improving. still seeing small cohort of clients failing (likely stuck resolvers).
Ops Lead: next if LB shift isn't enough: temporarily advertise a /32 via BGP to move the small fraction to healthy egress (manual hack). only if we see sustained errors after 10 minutes.
NetEng: BGP note: coordinate with peering ops, prep AS prep and withdraw scripts. example: `birdc` withdraw/announce quick commands.
Ben: cost note: scaling secondary pool from 3->7 increases committed GPU costs. call it out to finance if we keep it up >2h.
Maya: post-incident action item: run a TTL audit across zones, identify domains with >300s minimum TTL at common resolvers and document mitigations (LB weight, BGP, forced priming).
SRE Oncall: capturing logs and timeline, will open incident postmortem with root cause: resolver caching + incomplete LB fallback strategy + degraded apac GPU health.
Ops Lead: thank you everyone. keep the channel for updates only. if errors are stable for 15m we can start scaling down and revert LB weights. :white_check_mark:
